Tactical Map — Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific …
LAYERS
INFRASTRUCTURE
…
Map basis: Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection centred on 150 degrees east and 25 degrees south, drawn from Natural Earth country boundaries, state, region and province lines, rivers and sea labels. The frame runs from 105 degrees east to 202 degrees east (the Pacific is drawn across the date line, so Samoa, Tonga, Niue and the Cook Islands sit inside the region) and from 55 degrees south to 16 degrees north. Australia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Pacific states and the Indonesian islands are shaded; neighbouring countries are outlines. India is outside the frame and nothing about India is plotted. Disputed or contested areas are described, not settled: the Spratly Islands and Scarborough Reef (claimed by several states; outlined only), West Papua (Indonesian sovereignty, contested by insurgents), Bougainville (autonomy, with an independence vote pending in PNG's Parliament), and the Chatham and Cook islands' status as self-governing states in free association. Most positions are approximate; each tooltip gives its source and whether it is verified in this build. Incidents and displacement figures are reported claims. Events reflect reports up to 10 October 2026.

Darkweb & Threat Intel…
Sources: Ransomware.live (leak-site claims - group claims, not verified facts); Telegram threat-intel channels; and dark-web RSS sources reached through Tor that you verify yourself (data/onion_sources.json).
To read onion sources you need Tor on this PC: open Tor Browser (it listens on port 9150) or install and start the Tor service (port 9050). Keep it running, then press Refresh. Nothing is needed for the clear-web and Telegram sources. This dashboard never opens .onion pages in a browser and does not search or crawl the dark web.
